intro: Hollywood is LA's entertainment district, with historic movie palaces, the Walk of Fame, the Bowl and the Pantages, plus serious restaurants on Melrose, Highland and Sunset. Runyon Canyon and the hills around the Hollywood Sign start just above the flats.

to: Time Out: Best restaurants in Hollywood
todo: Time Out: Best things to do in Hollywood
gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites we checked)
barlis: Michelin Guide: Thompson Hollywood and Bar Lis

places.w: A bright new coffee bar with house-made syrups, plenty of seating, Wi-Fi and outlets.
places.o: A matcha with the pistachio blossom syrup or the apple pie latte.

places.w: A Yemeni coffeehouse near the Pantages, open late, with spiced lattes and rich desserts.
places.o: A Spanish latte and the Biscoff tres leches before a show.

places.w: The old 101 Coffee Shop space, revived by Clark Street Bread.
places.o: Blueberry pancakes or a hot sandwich. Open Wednesday through Sunday.

places.w: California-sourced cooking with a build-your-own breakfast.
places.o: The oatmeal griddle cakes.

places.w: Ludo Lefebvre's small, buzzy French bistro.
places.o: The Boursin omelet, steak frites or the Big Mec burger.

places.w: Hollywood's oldest restaurant, open since 1919, with red-jacketed waiters and a legendary martini.
places.o: A dry martini, a grilled steak and the flannel cakes.

places.w: Two-Michelin-star seafood tasting menus in a hushed room. One of LA's great splurges.
places.o: The full tasting menu.

places.w: Curtis Stone's Michelin-starred butcher shop and steakhouse with a fire-pit dining room.
places.o: A dry-aged steak and something from the butcher case to take home.

places.w: A European-style bistro in an old Hollywood haunt with an anything-goes energy.
places.o: Whatever's seasonal, and the dark chocolate tart.

places.w: Southern Thai home cooking from family recipes, with real heat.
places.o: The Phuket-style crab curry with rice noodles.

places.w: A Yucatán-inspired restaurant inside the Tommie hotel that feels like a resort.
places.o: Lamb neck barbacoa and a whole grilled fish.

places.w: A wellness-minded rooftop restaurant known for its happy hour.
places.o: The shiitake larb at happy hour.

places.w: A cocktail lounge inside the Hollywood Roosevelt with two antique bowling lanes.
places.o: A classic cocktail and a frame of bowling.

places.w: A 1970s house party of a bar, entered through a refrigerator door.
places.o: Head to the back patio for a boozy snow cone.

places.w: A hillside Japanese palace with one of the best views over Hollywood.
places.o: Book a window table at sunset.

places.w: LA's legendary outdoor amphitheater, where a summer picnic and concert is a rite of passage.
places.o: Bring a picnic and take the Bowl shuttle; parking is limited.

places.w: An Art Deco palace for touring Broadway musicals.
places.o: Front rows of the mezzanine are the best seats.

places.w: The historic movie palace with handprints in the forecourt and a giant IMAX screen.
places.o: Skip the crowded courtyard and see a movie in the main house.

places.w: A beautifully restored 1922 cinema for classics, cult films and festivals.
places.o: Catch a nitrate or 70mm screening.

places.w: Disney's movie palace with a live organ, a soda fountain and costume displays downstairs.
places.o: A Disney premiere with the kids.

places.w: A historic cemetery that hosts summer movie screenings, concerts and morning yoga.
places.o: Bring a blanket for a summer screening.

places.w: A great mid-size music hall with a rooftop bar over Hollywood Boulevard.
places.o: Get there early for the rooftop.

places.w: A big Art Deco ballroom for touring acts.
places.o: Check the calendar.

places.w: An intimate room for singer-songwriters.
places.o: A weeknight show in the main room.

places.w: A huge independent record store with vinyl, CDs and movies, plus free in-store shows.
places.o: Check the in-store calendar.

places.w: A private club for magicians in a Victorian mansion, with nightly shows.
places.o: Get in with a member, a hotel stay or show tickets.

places.w: A guided tram tour of the last major studio still in Hollywood.
places.o: Book ahead and download the tour app.

places.w: The famous sidewalk of stars. Expect crowds and souvenir shops.
places.o: Walk it early in the morning.

places.a: Sycamore Ave south of Romaine St
places.w: A small strip of restaurants, cafes and boutiques with galleries nearby.
places.o: Coffee, shopping, then the gallery on Orange Drive.

places.w: LA's most famous city hike, with dirt trails and big views right above Hollywood.
places.o: Go early; use the Mulholland entrance for an easier walk.

places.w: A grassy park with one of the closest, clearest views of the Hollywood Sign.
places.o: Photos of the sign, then a picnic.

places.w: A roadside lookout with wide views of the sign and the city.
places.o: Arrive early; it closes in the evening.

places.w: Guided horseback rides in Griffith Park with close views of the sign.
places.o: Book the sunset ride.

places.w: A French Riviera-style lounge on the roof of the Thompson Hollywood, with a straight view of the Hollywood Sign. Jazz on Tuesdays, a packed dance floor on Saturdays.
places.o: Come early for sunset, or book ahead on weekends when table minimums kick in.
